name: Permit consumption registry
purpose: Enforce controller-scoped, exactly-once permit consumption and bounded consumed-identity bookkeeping, returning explicit exhaustion results.
responsibilities: Record, atomically, the first consumption of a permit identity and of the bound session identity under a controller scope.
Reject a second consumption of the same permit identity even when the nonce has changed, via the consumed session-identity key.
Reject a permit already consumed for one session identity when presented for another session identity.
Bound the consumed-identity bookkeeping by a host-configured capacity and return CapacityExhausted rather than growing without limit.
Expose exact-set queries for tests and trace evidence without exposing a mutator.
state_ownership: Controller-scoped consumed-permit-identity set, bounded by max_consumed_permits.
Controller-scoped consumed-session-identity set, bounded by max_consumed_sessions.
Both sets guarded by the owning manager's single std::mutex; the registry is non-copyable and non-movable.
interfaces: try_consume(ControllerId, PermitId, SessionId, Result& out) -> Result (atomic check-then-insert)
capacity() const -> std::size_t; size() const -> std::size_t
concurrency: try_consume performs the full check-then-insert in one critical section, so N concurrent consumptions of one valid permit yield exactly one Ok and N-1 deterministic failures.
errors: SessionAlreadyConsumed: session identity already bound to a consumed permit.
CapacityExhausted: consumed-identity bookkeeping is full and the consumption is refused.
deployment: Compiled in the standalone candidate; keyed sets use std::array-backed open-addressing with a fixed capacity to guarantee bounded memory.
rationale: Keeping consumption bookkeeping separate from the session table makes the exactly-once rule and its bounded exhaustion behavior independently testable and traceable to SR-009 and SR-010.
